##### label encoding #####
bank.$y <- ifelse(bank.$y == "yes", 1, 0)
bank.$Housing_loan <- ifelse(bank.$Housing.loan == "yes", 1, 0)
bank.$Personal_loan <- ifelse(bank.$Personal.loan == "yes", 1, 0)
bank.$Default_status <- ifelse(bank.$Default == "yes", 1, 0)

##### packages ##### ---> install ---> search the package ####
library(fastDummies)
bank. = dummy_cols(bank.,select_columns = c("Job.profile", "Marital.status", "Education", "Contact.type", "previous.campaign.outcome"))
summary(bank.)

#### Step-4 Training and testing ####
library(caTools)
set.seed(111)
split = sample.split(bank.$y,SplitRatio = 0.7)
trainingbank. = subset(bank., split=="TRUE")
testingbank. = subset(bank., split=="FALSE")

write.csv(cr,"bank._cor.csv")
getwd()
## [1] "C:/Users/Win11/OneDrive/Desktop"
#### Step-5 Built model on training data
library(car)
## Loading required package: carData
# Model 1: Single economic baseline feature
model1= glm(y ~  Euro.Interbank.offered.rate, data=trainingbank., family = binomial)
summary(model1)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = y ~ Euro.Interbank.offered.rate, family = binomial, 
##     data = trainingbank.)
## 
## Coefficients:
##                             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)                 -0.46968    0.03283  -14.30   <2e-16 ***
## Euro.Interbank.offered.rate -0.54033    0.01147  -47.12   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 20299  on 28831  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 17714  on 28830  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 17718
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 5
# Model 2: Adding Consumer Price Index
model2 = glm(y ~ Euro.Interbank.offered.rate + consumer.price.index, data=trainingbank., family = binomial)
summary(model2)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = y ~ Euro.Interbank.offered.rate + consumer.price.index, 
##     family = binomial, data = trainingbank.)
##

model14 = glm(y ~ Euro.Interbank.offered.rate + consumer.price.index + campaign + `previous.campaign.outcome_success` + age + `Job.profile_blue-collar` + consumer.confidence.index + pdays + Housing_loan + Personal_loan + `Job.profile_retired` + `Job.profile_student` + `Education_university.degree` + `Contact.type_cellular`, data=trainingbank., family = binomial)
summary(model14)

### STEP 6: ROCR Curve to decide the cutoff### 
library(ROCR)
ROCRpred = prediction(res,testingbank.$y) ### TN TP FP FN

plot(ROCRpref,colorize=TRUE,print.cutoffs.at=seq(0.2,by=0.1))
